very_low_decisions.reason: Unobserved species, stage and depth composition spans all represented bony-fish groups 6–19. The reporting functional tag does not restrict the set to demersal fish. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.
Pacific herring provides a coastal schooling pelagic-fish analogue. Scombrid lineage, greater piscivory and slope use differ; literal mackerel membership is absent. Allocation is 100% to herring.

Source Salmon supplies a mobile marine water-column fish analogue. Its pooled diet is predominantly zooplanktivorous, and it has no species/size inventory establishing a large-pelagic-predator guild. Lineage, size, residency and habitat mismatches remain; each taxon receives 100% in Salmon.
Capelin provides a schooling pelagic zooplanktivorous analogue. Saury oceanic/migratory ecology and beloniform lineage differ. Allocation is 100% to capelin.

Squids and carnivorous benthos approximate pelagic and benthic cephalopods. Octopus/cuttlefish/argonaut components are not literal listed squid members; habitat and lineage composition is unknown. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.

Herring and Salmon provide coastal-schooling and mobile marine-fish analogues for absent mackerel, tuna, bonito and billfish components. Lineage and historical reporting scope differ; constituent shares are unobserved. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.
Pacific Sardine provides a schooling clupeoid plankton-filtering analogue. Engraulid identity differs and the source sardine binomial is unverified. Allocation is 100% to sardine.

Crabs and shrimps plus inferred crustacean components of benthos and zooplankton approximate this broad label. Residual pools also contain non-crustaceans; constituent shares are unknown. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.
Source Salmon is not an exhaustive salmonid-family inventory. Trout, char and whitefish introduce unrepresented freshwater habitats and feeding modes into the broad-family approximation.

No cartilage compartment is represented. Pollock, Salmon, residual bottom fish and mesopelagic fish form a weak habitat/predatory-fish analogue union; lineage, body form and constituent shares differ. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.

Crabs and shrimps and Carnivorous invertebrates provide competing benthic crustacean/feeding analogues. No inventory establishes literal lobster or mantis-shrimp membership; lineage, feeding pooling and lobster shallow-water transfer remain uncertain. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.

Unknown composition can span named and residual benthic and pelagic invertebrate guilds. No source inventory or catch composition establishes the broad reporting mixture. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.

Other bottom fishes provides a substrate-associated fish analogue. The model lacks a grazing/detritivorous fish group; feeding mode, reef/brackish habitat and lineage differ. Allocation is 100% to this analogue.

Historical perch-like reporting crosses present-day taxonomy and habitats. Cottidae, Ammodytidae and residual fish pools are supplemented by herring/Salmon analogues for absent mackerels/jacks; herring is not a literal perch-like member. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.

Squids and basal/carnivorous benthos approximate clams, seasnails and cephalopods. Residual benthos lacks an exhaustive species list, and whole-phylum composition is unobserved. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.

Unknown composition is approximated across named pelagic, benthopelagic and mesopelagic fish. Explicit bottom-fish pools are excluded; the remaining union is not a measured catch composition. Split weights use source biomass with equal catchability assumed; fixed 1980s composition is transferred across catch years and bases.
Pacific herring provides a pelagic zooplankton/gelatinous-prey fish analogue. Giant size, nonschooling gelatinivory and lineage differ. Allocation is 100% to herring.
Pacific herring provides a schooling pelagic planktivore/gelatinous-prey fish analogue. Family identity, feeding and size differ. Allocation is 100% to herring.
Pacific Sardine provides a coastal schooling plankton/detritus-feeding analogue. Milkfish lineage, tropical/brackish habitat and body size differ. Allocation is 100% to sardine.

Other bottom fishes provides a benthic predatory-fish analogue for skates/rays. The model has no cartilage pool; bony lineage, body form and habitat breadth differ. Allocation is 100% to this analogue.
Salmon provides a cold-water salmonid analogue. Freshwater/brackish life histories and feeding differ from the marine stock; the caught aquatic mode is unknown. Allocation is 100% to Salmon.
